docs.title: Multi-fidelity Multi-point SBO
docs.text:
A framework for surrogate-based optimisation (SBO) with asynchronous multi-point and/or multi-fidelity infill strategies, developed for the MSc thesis Combining an Asynchronous Multi-Point and a Multi-Fidelity Infill Strategy for Surrogate-Based Optimisation.

Version 1.0.0 is the code exactly as used for the thesis results. It is not actively developed: known limitations and unfinished parts are listed under Included Algorithms, and issues and pull requests may not get a response.

The package implements Efficient Global Optimisation (EGO): a surrogate model is fitted to the samples evaluated so far, an infill strategy uses the surrogate to choose where to sample next, and an optimisation algorithm drives this loop until a stopping criterion is met. On top of standard single-point EGO it supports:

  • Multi-point infill: several points are evaluated in parallel with MPI, either synchronously (EgoMPI) or asynchronously (EgoAsync), where a new point is proposed as soon as a worker is free.
  • Multi-fidelity optimisation: cheaper, lower-fidelity version(s) of the objective are combined with the expensive high-fidelity function to reduce the number of expensive evaluations.
  • Verified implementations: the main surrogates, infill strategies and optimisers are checked against reference implementations.
  • HPC: an Apptainer container for running on a cluster with the host's MPI.

docs.title: Thesis Results
docs.text:
The thesis benchmarked the strategies on eleven two-fidelity test functions and compared them with sequential, single-fidelity EGO (Kriging and Expected Improvement), using the expected runtime (ERT) to reach the optimum:

  • Asynchronous multi-point (16 MPI processes: 1 coordinator and 15 workers): the ERT dropped by 72.7%, a statistically significant improvement.
  • Multi-fidelity (hierarchical Kriging with TwoStep, single-point): the ERT increased by 21.2%.
  • Both combined: the ERT dropped by 68.2%, so the multi-fidelity part cost some of the multi-point gain.

The multi-fidelity strategy added redundant low-fidelity samples near the optimum, because TwoStep reselects the sample location based on the residual variance of the hierarchical Kriging model. Tests with eleven different low-fidelity versions of the Forrester function showed that this is structural, not caused by one particular low-fidelity function. Adapting the fidelity-selection threshold during the optimisation, or using a different multi-fidelity criterion, are the most promising ways to gain from combining both.

Change in ERT relative to sequential, single-fidelity EGO with Kriging and EI (SF: single-fidelity, MF: multi-fidelity, SP: single-point, Async: asynchronous multi-point, n: number of MPI processes). The full results are in the thesis.

Surrogate-Based Optimisation (SBO) class.

This class is the entry-point for the end-user to perform surrogate-based optimisation, using any combination of the supported surrogate models, infill strategies and optimisation algorithms.

The SBO class initialises the specified components based on the provided configuration and orchestrates the optimisation process.

To use the SBO class, create an instance with a Config object and call the run method to execute the optimisation process. The optimum solution can be accessed via the optimum property or by calling the instance directly.

Attributes:

Name Type Description config 
The configuration object containing settings for the SBO process.

_infill The infill strategy component. _surrogate The surrogate model component. _optimisation The optimisation algorithm component. _optimum The optimum solution found by the SBO process.

Examples:

>>> config = Config(...)
>>> sbo = SBO(config)
>>> optimum = sbo()  # or sbo.run()

def __init__(
    self, config: Config, *args, initial_samples: list[dict] | None = None, **kwargs
) -> None:
    """Initialise the SBO class.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config
        The configuration object containing settings for the SBO process.
    initial_samples
        Optional initial samples to set in the surrogate model.
    """
    self.config: Config = config
    self._optimum: dict | None = None

    self._infill: InfillBase = self._initialise_component(
        *args,
        algorithm=self.config.used_algorithms["infill"],
        algorithm_type="infill",
        config=self.config,
        **kwargs,
    )
    self._surrogate: SurrogateBase = self._initialise_component(
        *args,
        algorithm=self.config.used_algorithms["surrogate"],
        algorithm_type="surrogate",
        config=self.config,
        **kwargs,
    )
    self._optimisation: OptimisationBase = self._initialise_component(
        *args,
        algorithm=self.config.used_algorithms["optimisation"],
        algorithm_type="optimisation",
        config=self.config,
        **kwargs,
    )

    # Take the backup only after the components are created: a component can
    # replace itself (e.g. HK -> KRG for a single fidelity) and update
    # config.used_algorithms. Taking the backup earlier would make run() see a
    # change and rebuild the surrogate without its initial samples.
    self._backup_used_alg: dict = copy.deepcopy(self.config.used_algorithms)

    # Set initial samples if provided else samples using LHS
    if MPI is None or MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank() == 0:
        self.config.logger.info(f"Dealing with initial samples with MPI: {MPI}")
        if MPI is not None:
            self.config.logger.info(f"Current rank = {MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank()}")
        if not initial_samples:
            initial_samples = self._get_initial_samples()
        else:
            initial_samples = self._ensure_enough_initial_samples(initial_samples)

        # If MPI is used, send initial samples to other ranks
        if MPI is not None:
            initial_samples = MPI.COMM_WORLD.bcast(initial_samples, root=0)

    # If MPI is used, receive initial samples from root
    elif MPI is not None and MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank() != 0:
        initial_samples = MPI.COMM_WORLD.bcast(initial_samples, root=0)

    if MPI is not None:
        self.config.logger.debug(
            f"Initial samples on rank {MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank()}: "
            f"{initial_samples}"
        )
    self._surrogate.set_training_data(initial_samples)

def run(self) -> dict:
    """Execute the SBO process and return the optimum solution.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The optimum solution point ({'coord': np.ndarray, 'value': float}).
    """
    if self.config.used_algorithms != self._backup_used_alg:
        self.update_used_algorithms(self.config.used_algorithms)

    # For not rank==0 optimisation no points need to be processed.
    if MPI is not None and MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank() != 0:
        self._optimisation(surrogate=self._surrogate, infill=self._infill)
        return {}

    if (
        max(
            [
                len(self._surrogate.samples[fid])
                for fid in self._surrogate.samples.keys()
            ]
        )
        <= 1
    ):
        self.config.logger.warning(
            "Tried calling SBO run, without any samples in surrogate."
        )
        self._surrogate.set_training_data(self._get_initial_samples())

    self._optimum = self._optimisation(
        surrogate=self._surrogate, infill=self._infill
    )
    return self._optimum

def update_used_algorithms(self, new_used_alg: dict) -> None:
    """Update the used algorithms.

    Parameters
    ----------
    new_used_alg
        new used algorithms dictionary
        (required keys: infill, surrogate, optimisation)
    """
    for key, new_alg in new_used_alg.items():
        if key not in self.config.used_algorithms.keys():
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"Algorithm '{key}' not a valid key, ignoring."
            )
            continue

        # Test if not the same type, if so continue
        if new_alg == self._backup_used_alg[key]:
            continue

        self._backup_used_alg[key] = new_alg
        self.config.update_used_algorithms(copy.deepcopy(self._backup_used_alg))

        if key == "optimisation":
            self._optimisation = self._initialise_component(
                algorithm=new_alg,
                algorithm_type=key,
                config=self.config,
            )
        elif key == "surrogate":
            # Keep the training data of the old surrogate
            old_samples = copy.deepcopy(self._surrogate.samples)
            self._surrogate = self._initialise_component(
                algorithm=new_alg,
                algorithm_type=key,
                config=self.config,
            )
            if any(old_samples.values()):
                self._surrogate.set_training_data(old_samples)
        elif key == "infill":
            self._infill = self._initialise_component(
                algorithm=new_alg,
                algorithm_type=key,
                config=self.config,
            )

    # A component can replace itself on creation (e.g. HK -> KRG) and update
    # config.used_algorithms, so sync the backup with the config afterwards.
    self._backup_used_alg = copy.deepcopy(self.config.used_algorithms)

    """Plot the surrogate model for 1D and 2D problems for iteration or timestep.

    Exposed method for plotting the surrogates.

    Parameters
    ----------
    title
        The title for the plot.
    filename
        The filename to save the plot to. If None, the plot will not be saved.
        If a relative path is provided, the relative path from the output directory
        will be used.

        from all fidelities will be plotted. If no sample points are to be plotted,
        set to an empty list.

Default settings used in all optimisation algorithms.

The convergence criteria compare the optimum of the surrogate model (the minimum of the HF surrogate prediction, 'surrogate_optimum' in the optimisation data), not the best observed sample value. This is intended: the surrogate optimum also changes when new samples change the model, while the best observed value only changes when a better sample is found.

Keys: - 'convergence_threshold': float | None, threshold for convergence if None this will not be considered (default: 1e-6, must be >= 0.0) (abs(surrogate optimum 'convergence_window' iterations ago - current surrogate optimum) < convergence_threshold) - 'convergence_window': int | None, number of iterations to consider for convergence. Calculated as the difference between the surrogate optimum of the current iteration and the surrogate optimum 'convergence_window' iterations ago. Used to determine if the optimisation has converged, based on the convergence_threshold and relative_convergence_threshold. (default: 5, must be >= 1) - 'constant_liar_lie': str, the type of lie to use in the Constant Liar algorithm. (default: "min", allowed: ["min", "max", "mean"]) - 'max_function_calls': int | None, maximum number of function calls (all fidelities), if None this stopping criterion will not be used. One HF call is reserved for the final evaluation of the surrogate optimum, which is included. (default: 1000, must be >= 1) - 'max_function_calls_HF': int | None, maximum number of function calls for high fidelity, if None this stopping criterion will not be used. One call is reserved for the final evaluation of the surrogate optimum, which is included. (default: 150, must be >= 1) - 'max_iterations': int | None, maximum number of iterations, if None this stopping criterion will not be used. Not used by EgoAsync, which has no iterations. (default: 300, must be >= 1) - 'min_infill_value': float | None, minimum value for the infill criterion, if None this stopping criterion will not be used. (default: 1e-6, must be >= 0.0) - 'multipoint_algorithm': str, the algorithm to use for multipoint selection if the surrogate has not yet received the new points. 1. "KB" for Kriging Believer (default) 2. "CL" for Constant Liar (default: "KB", allowed: ["KB", "CL"]) - 'relative_convergence_threshold': float | None, relative threshold for convergence, if None this stopping criterion will not be used. abs(surrogate optimum 'convergence_window' iterations ago - current surrogate optimum) / abs(surrogate optimum 'convergence_window' iterations ago) < relative_convergence_threshold (default: 1e-6, must be >= 0.0)

def get_new_points(
    self,
    surrogate: SurrogateBaseWithVariance | SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity,
    fidelity: int = 0,
) -> tuple[list[list[dict]], float]:
    """Generate new points based on the Constrained Expected Improvement strategy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    surrogate
        The surrogate model used to evaluate the infill strategy.
    fidelity
        The fidelity level to sample at (default: 0, high-fidelity). Only possible
        with SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[list[list[dict]], float]
        The new points and the infill value. The new points are a list of
        tasks; each task is a list of points to evaluate together
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, 'fid': int}, fid 0 is HF). The infill value is
        the value of the infill criterion at the selected point.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the surrogate does not provide variance estimates, or a lower fidelity is
        requested from a surrogate without variance per fidelity.
    """
    # EI only supports surrogates with variance estimates
    if not isinstance(
        surrogate, SurrogateBaseWithVariance | SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity
    ):
        self.config.logger.error(
            "surrogate model must provide variance estimates for CEI calculation."
        )
        raise TypeError(
            "surrogate model must provide variance estimates for CEI calculation."
        )

    if fidelity != 0 and not isinstance(
        surrogate, SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity
    ):
        msg = (
            "surrogate does not support variance per fidelity required for "
            "sampling at lower fidelities."
        )
        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise TypeError(msg)

    # Calculate the best point to sample (maximising CEI) with the shared
    # infill optimisation of the base class
    best_value = min(p["value"] for p in surrogate.samples[fidelity])
    coord, neg_cei_value = self._select_sample_point_optimisation(
        lambda x: -self.calc_infill_value(
            np.atleast_2d(x), surrogate, best_value=best_value, fidelity=fidelity
        ),
        constraints=self.config.scipy_constraints(),
    )

    task = [{"coord": coord, "fid": 0}]
    return [self._return_nested_samples(task)], -neg_cei_value

        surrogate, SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity

        msg = (

            "sampling at lower fidelities."

        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise TypeError(msg)

    if fidelity < 0 or fidelity >= self.config.num_fidelities:
        self.config.logger.error(
            "Invalid fidelity level provided for EI calculation."
        )
        raise ValueError("Invalid fidelity level provided for EI calculation.")

    if best_value is None:
        # Get the best function value from the surrogate model if not provided
        try:
            best_value = min(
                [p["value"] for p in surrogate.samples.get(fidelity, {})]
            )
        except ValueError as e:
            self.config.logger.error(
                "No samples found in surrogate model to determine best value for "
                f"EI calculation. Exit with error: {e}"
            )
            raise ValueError(
                "No samples found in surrogate model to determine best value for "
                f"EI calculation. Exit with error: {e}"
            )

        x, surrogate, *args, best_value=best_value, fidelity=fidelity, **kwargs
    )

def calc_infill_value(
    self,
    x: np.ndarray,
    surrogate: SurrogateBaseWithVariance | SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity,
    *args,
    best_value: float | None = None,
    fidelity: int = 0,
    **kwargs,
) -> float:
    """Calculate EI value. Accepts optional keyword-only `best_value`.

    `best_value` can be provided by callers of EI; if not provided it can be
    obtained from `context`/`kwargs` or computed from the surrogate.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x
        The coordinates of the point to evaluate.
    surrogate
        The surrogate model used to evaluate the infill strategy.
    best_value
        The best known objective function value. If None, it will be obtained
        from the surrogate model if possible.
    fidelity
        The fidelity level to sample at (default: 0, high-fidelity). Only possible
        when surrogate is SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The Expected Improvement value at the given point.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the surrogate does not provide variance estimates, or a lower fidelity is
        requested from a surrogate without variance per fidelity.
    ValueError
        If the fidelity level is invalid, or no samples are available to determine
        the best value.
    """
    # Check if surrogate provides variance estimates
    if not isinstance(
        surrogate, SurrogateBaseWithVariance | SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity
    ):
        self.config.logger.error(
            "surrogate model must provide variance estimates for EI calculation."
        )
        raise TypeError(
            "surrogate model must provide variance estimates for EI calculation."
        )

    if fidelity != 0 and not isinstance(
        surrogate, SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity
    ):
        msg = (
            "surrogate does not support variance per fidelity required for "
            "sampling at lower fidelities."
        )
        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise TypeError(msg)

    if fidelity < 0 or fidelity >= self.config.num_fidelities:
        self.config.logger.error(
            "Invalid fidelity level provided for EI calculation."
        )
        raise ValueError("Invalid fidelity level provided for EI calculation.")

    if best_value is None:
        # Get the best function value from the surrogate model if not provided
        try:
            best_value = min(
                [p["value"] for p in surrogate.samples.get(fidelity, {})]
            )
        except ValueError as e:
            self.config.logger.error(
                "No samples found in surrogate model to determine best value for "
                f"EI calculation. Exit with error: {e}"
            )
            raise ValueError(
                "No samples found in surrogate model to determine best value for "
                f"EI calculation. Exit with error: {e}"
            )

    mu, variance = surrogate(
        np.atleast_2d(x), return_variance=True, fidelity=fidelity
    )
    neg_tol = -1e-5
    if np.any(variance < neg_tol):
        self.config.logger.debug(
            "Surrogate returned significant negative variance."
        )
    variance = np.maximum(variance, 0.0)
    sigma = np.sqrt(variance)
    if np.all(np.abs(sigma) <= 1e-12):
        return 0.0

    improvement = best_value - mu
    has_variance = sigma > 1e-12
    # Avoid dividing by zero; points without variance get z = 0 (overwritten)
    z = np.divide(
        improvement,
        sigma,
        out=np.zeros_like(improvement, dtype=float),
        where=has_variance,
    )

    ei = improvement * norm.cdf(z) + sigma * norm.pdf(z)
    # Without variance the expected improvement is the (positive) improvement
    ei = np.where(has_variance, ei, np.maximum(improvement, 0.0))
    ei = ei.flatten()

    if len(ei) == 1:
        return float(ei[0])
    return ei

def get_new_points(
    self,
    surrogate: CoKRG,
    *args,
    samples_per_iteration: None | dict[int, list[float]] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[list[list[dict]], float]:
    """Generate new points based on the Filtered GEI strategy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    surrogate
        The CoKriging surrogate model.
    samples_per_iteration
        A dictionary where keys are iteration indices and values are lists of
        sampled high-fidelity values in that iteration. If None, the mean of all
        high-fidelity samples will be used for threshold calculation.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[list[list[dict]], float]
        The new points and the infill value. The new points are a list of
        tasks; each task is a list of points to evaluate together
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, 'fid': int}, fid 0 is HF). The infill value is
        the value of the infill criterion at the selected point.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the surrogate is not a CoKRG surrogate.
    ValueError
        If the surrogate has more than 2 fidelity levels.
    """
    if not isinstance(surrogate, CoKRG):
        self.config.logger.error("surrogate must be of type CoKRG.")
        raise TypeError("surrogate must be of type CoKRG")
    if surrogate.config.num_fidelities > 2:
        self.config.logger.error("FilteredGEI only supports 2 fidelity levels.")
        raise ValueError("FilteredGEI only supports 2 fidelity levels.")

    # Determine the sample location using GEI
    best_value = surrogate.get_optimum()["value"]
    x_location, neg_gei_value = self._select_sample_point_optimisation(
        lambda x: -self.calc_infill_value(x, surrogate, best_value=best_value)
    )
    x_location = np.asarray(x_location)
    gei_value = -neg_gei_value

    # Determine whether to sample HF or LF based on threshold
    threshold = self._calc_threshold(
        surrogate, x_location.reshape(1, -1), best_value, samples_per_iteration
    )[0]

    if surrogate.predict(x_location, return_variance=False)[0] < threshold:
        fid = 0  # Sample HF
    else:
        fid = 1

    task = [{"coord": x_location, "fid": fid}]
    return [self._return_nested_samples(task)], gei_value

def calc_infill_value(
    self,
    x: np.ndarray,
    surrogate: SurrogateBaseWithVariance,
    *args,
    best_value: float | None = None,
    fidelity: int = 0,
    **kwargs,
) -> float:
    """Calculate the Generalised Expected Improvement (GEI) value at a given point.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x
        The input point where the GEI is to be calculated.
    surrogate
        The surrogate model used to estimate the objective function.
    best_value
        The current best-known value of the objective function. If None, it will be
        retrieved from the surrogate model.
    fidelity
        The fidelity level at which to evaluate the surrogate model.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The calculated GEI value at the input point.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the surrogate does not provide variance estimates.
    """
    if best_value is None:
        # Get the best function value from the surrogate model if not provided
        best_value = surrogate.get_optimum()["value"]

    if not isinstance(surrogate, SurrogateBaseWithVariance):
        msg = "surrogate model must provide variance estimates for GEI calculation."
        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise TypeError(msg)

    mu, variance = surrogate(
        np.atleast_2d(x), return_variance=True, fidelity=fidelity
    )
    neg_tol = -1e-5
    if np.any(variance < neg_tol):
        self.config.logger.error(
            "Surrogate returned significant negative variance."
        )
    variance = np.maximum(variance, 0.0)
    sigma = np.sqrt(variance)
    if np.all(np.abs(sigma) <= 1e-12):
        return 0.0

    u = (best_value - mu) / sigma
    t = [norm.cdf(u), -norm.pdf(u)]
    g = self.config.get("infill.g")

    for k in range(2, g + 1):
        tk = -(u ** (k - 1)) * norm.pdf(u) + (k - 1) * t[-2]
        t.append(tk)

    gei = np.zeros_like(mu)
    for k in range(g + 1):
        gei += (-1) ** k * comb(g, k) * (u ** (g - k)) * t[k]
    gei *= sigma**g

    gei = gei.flatten()
    if len(gei) == 1:
        return float(gei[0])
    return gei

def get_new_points(self, *args, **kwargs) -> tuple[list[list[dict]], float]:
    """Generate new random points within the defined bounds.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[list[list[dict]], float]
        The new points and the infill value. The new points are a list of
        tasks; each task is a list of points to evaluate together
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, 'fid': int}, fid 0 is HF). The infill value is
        always inf for Random.
    """
    number_new_points = self.config["number_new_points"]

    new_points = self.config.rng.uniform(
        low=self.config.lb,
        high=self.config.ub,
        size=(number_new_points, self.config.dimension),
    )
    if self.config.num_fidelities > 1:
        fidelities = self.config.rng.integers(
            low=0,
            high=self.config.num_fidelities,
            size=(number_new_points,),
            dtype=int,
        )
    else:
        fidelities = np.zeros((number_new_points,), dtype=int)

    # Create list of new points with fidelity levels
    new_points = [
        self._return_nested_samples(
            [{"coord": new_points[i], "fid": fidelities[i]}]
        )
        for i in range(len(new_points))
    ]

    return new_points, float("inf")

This method utilises a two-step approach to determine the next sampling point: 1. Determine the sample location based on a single-fidelity infill strategy 2. Determine the cheapest accurate enough fidelity to sample at that location, based on the Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) between the high-fidelity (HF) surrogate and each lower-fidelity surrogate at the selected location.

The method is introduced by Garbo et al. [1].

This infill strategy is designed to work with a surrogate model that provides both predictions of the mean and uncertainty (variance) of the function values.

def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
    """Initialise the TwoStep infill strategy.

    The single-fidelity infill strategy used to determine the sample location is
    read from the ``infill.single_fid_infill`` setting of the config.

    Raises
    ------
    ImportError
        If the single-fidelity infill strategy can not be found or created.
    """
    # Initialise the InfillBase class
    super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

    # Configure the single fidelity infill strategy
    single_fid_name = self.config.get("infill.single_fid_infill")

    # Load the single-fidelity infill strategy dynamically
    base_module = importlib.import_module("..infill", package=__package__)
    attr = getattr(base_module, single_fid_name, None)

    # If attribute is a module, import the submodule and search for a suitable class
    if inspect.ismodule(attr):
        submodule = importlib.import_module(
            f"..infill.{single_fid_name}", package=__package__
        )
        cls = getattr(submodule, single_fid_name, None)
    else:
        cls = attr

    if cls is None or not inspect.isclass(cls):
        msg = (
            f"Single-fidelity infill strategy class '{single_fid_name}' "
            f"not found or is not a class in module '{base_module.__name__}'"
        )
        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise ImportError(msg)

    # Instantiate the infill strategy
    try:
        self.single_fid_infill = cls(config=self.config)
    except (TypeError, AttributeError) as e:
        msg = (
            f"Error initialising single-fidelity infill strategy "
            f"'{single_fid_name}': {e}"
        )
        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise ImportError(msg)

def get_new_points(
    self, surrogate: SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity
) -> tuple[list[list[dict]], float]:
    """Generate new points based on the two-step approach.

    Parameters
    ----------
    surrogate
        The surrogate model used to evaluate the infill strategy.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[list[list[dict]], float]
        The new points and the infill value. The new points are a list of
        tasks; each task is a list of points to evaluate together
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, 'fid': int}, fid 0 is HF). The infill value is
        the value of the infill criterion at the selected point.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the surrogate does not provide variance estimates per fidelity.
    """
    if not isinstance(surrogate, SurrogateBaseWithVariancePerFidelity):
        self.config.logger.error(
            "TwoStep infill strategy requires a surrogate model that provides "
            "uncertainty estimates per fidelity."
        )
        raise ValueError(
            "TwoStep infill strategy requires a surrogate model that provides "
            "uncertainty estimates per fidelity."
        )

    # Step 1: Determine the sample location using the single-fidelity infill
    samples, infill_value = self.single_fid_infill(surrogate)
    x_new = samples[0][0]["coord"]  # Extract the coordinates of the new point

    # Step 2: Determine the cheapest accurate enough fidelity at that location
    accurate_fidelities = self._get_accurate_enough_fidelities(x_new, surrogate)
    cheapest_fidelity = max(accurate_fidelities)  # LF has higher index

    new_samples = [{"coord": x_new, "fid": cheapest_fidelity}]
    return [self._return_nested_samples(new_samples)], infill_value

def evaluate_point(
    self, point: dict, inplace: bool = False, bypass_delay: bool = False
) -> dict:
    """Evaluate a given point using the objective function.

    Parameters
    ----------
    point
        A dictionary containing the point to be evaluated.
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, "fid": int})
    inplace
        If True, the evaluation result is added to the input point dictionary.
        If False, a new dictionary is returned with the evaluation result.
    bypass_delay
        If True, the delay specified will be skipped.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A dictionary containing the evaluated point and its objective value.
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, "fid": int, 'value': float})
    """
    # Add starting time to point if not already present
    if inplace:
        if "start_time" not in point:
            point["start_time"] = time.time()
        if MPI is not None:
            point["mpi_rank"] = MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank()
        else:
            point["mpi_rank"] = 0
    elif not inplace:
        evaluated_point = copy.deepcopy(point)
        if "start_time" not in evaluated_point:
            evaluated_point["start_time"] = time.time()
        if MPI is not None:
            evaluated_point["mpi_rank"] = MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank()
        else:
            evaluated_point["mpi_rank"] = 0

    fidelity = point["fid"]
    func = self.config.functions[fidelity]
    value = func(point["coord"])[0]
    if inplace:
        point["value"] = value
    else:
        evaluated_point["value"] = value

    # Pause if a function delay is set
    function_delay = self.config.get("function_delay", None)
    if function_delay is not None and not bypass_delay:
        if len(function_delay) == 0:
            delay = None
        elif fidelity < len(function_delay):
            delay = function_delay[fidelity]
        else:
            # Fewer delays than fidelities: use the delay of the last fidelity
            delay = function_delay[-1]
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"No function delay given for fidelity {fidelity} "
                f"(function_delay has {len(function_delay)} entries); using the "
                f"last value ({delay} s)."
            )
        if delay is None:
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"No function delay found for fidelity {fidelity}. "
                "No delay will be applied."
            )
        else:
            time.sleep(delay)

    if inplace:
        point["end_time"] = time.time()
        return point
    else:
        evaluated_point["end_time"] = time.time()
        return evaluated_point

Class implementing Asynchronous Efficient Global Optimisation (EGO).

This class implements the Asynchronous EGO algorithm, which samples new points based on a specified infill strategy. These points are selected on the coordinator process and the generated task is sent to an available worker process for evaluation. Once the worker process has completed the evaluation, the results are sent back to the coordinator process, which updates the surrogate model with the new data. The optimisation continues until a stopping criterion is met. If the surrogate is not updated a new point can not be selected since it will select a pending point. To resolve this issue, either the kriging Believer (KB) or Constant Liar (CL) multi-point algorithm is used to generate new points, using the existing surrogate and pending points.

def solve(
    self, surrogate: SurrogateBase, infill: InfillBase, *args, **kwargs
) -> dict | None:
    """Run the Asynchronous EGO Optimisation algorithm.

    Parameters
    ----------
    surrogate
        Surrogate model to use for optimisation.
    infill
        Infill strategy to use for selecting new points.

    Returns
    -------
    dict | None
        The best point found on the coordinator process, None on worker processes.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If fewer than 2 MPI processes are available (EgoAsync needs a coordinator
        and at least one worker).
    """
    # Test if enough MPI processes are available
    if self.mpi_size < 2:
        msg = "EgoAsync requires at least 2 MPI processes."
        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    # Solve as coordinator or worker based on MPI rank
    if self.mpi_rank == 0:
        optimum = self._solve_coordinator(surrogate, infill)
    else:
        optimum = self._solve_worker()
    return optimum

        The surrogate model used to approximate the objective function.
    infill
        The infill strategy used to select new points to evaluate.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The best point found, as a dictionary with keys "value", "coord", and "fid".
    """
    if MPI is not None and MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank() != 0:
        self.config.logger.info(
            "EGO Sequential Optimisation is only run on the root process."
        )
        return None

    # Save initial state to optimisation data
    self._optimisation_data["init"] = {
        "best_coord": None,
        "best_value": None,
        "infill_value": None,
        "function_calls": None,
        "function_calls_HF": None,
        "sample_points": copy.deepcopy(surrogate.samples),
        "time_elapsed": None,
        "surrogate_optimum": None,
    }

    # Setup counters and timers
    iteration = 0
    best_point = {"value": float("inf"), "coord": None, "fid": None}
    start_time = time.time()
    function_calls = dict.fromkeys(range(self.config.num_fidelities), 0)
    prev_surr_opt = {"value": float("inf"), "coord": None, "fid": None}

    # Start optimisation loop
    self.config.logger.info("Starting EGO Sequential Optimisation")
    while True:
        self.config.logger.info(f"Iteration {iteration} started")

        # Setup timer for the iteration and save previous best value
        iter_start_time = time.time()
        prev_best = best_point

        # get new points to evaluate
        new_points, infill_value = infill(surrogate)

        # Check if new points not already sampled, if so remove from tasks:
        new_points = self._remove_duplicates(new_points, surrogate)

        # Evaluate the new points sequentially
        for task in new_points:
            for point in task:
                self.evaluate_point(point, inplace=True)
                function_calls[point["fid"]] += 1

        # Flatten points list and add to the surrogate model
        evaluated_points = [point for task in new_points for point in task]
        surrogate.add_training_data(evaluated_points)
        surrogate.train()

        # Get the current best value
        best_point = min(surrogate.samples[0], key=lambda p: p["value"])
        curr_surr_opt = {**surrogate.get_optimum(fidelity=0), "fid": 0}

        # Save the data and calculate stopping criteria
        stop = self._run_end_iteration(
            iteration=iteration,
            function_calls=function_calls,
            best_val=best_point["value"],
            prev_best_val=prev_best["value"],
            infill_value=infill_value,
            best_coord=best_point["coord"],
            surrogate=surrogate,
            start_time_iteration=iter_start_time,
            current_surrogate_optimum=curr_surr_opt,
            prev_surrogate_optimum=prev_surr_opt,
        )

        # if stopping criteria met, break the loop
        if stop:
            break

        # Update iteration counter
        self.config.logger.info(f"Iteration {iteration} finished")
        iteration += 1

        # Update the prev best points
        prev_surr_opt = curr_surr_opt

    # Calculate the best point, add to dict
    best_point = min(surrogate.samples[0], key=lambda p: p["value"])
    surr_opt = {**surrogate.get_optimum(), "fid": 0}
    surr_opt = self.evaluate_point(surr_opt, inplace=False, bypass_delay=True)
    self._count_final_evaluation(function_calls)
    if surr_opt["value"] < best_point["value"]:
        best_point = surr_opt
    self._optimisation_data.setdefault("solution", None)
    self._optimisation_data["solution"] = best_point
    self._optimisation_data["total"]["best_coord"] = best_point["coord"]
    self._optimisation_data["total"]["best_value"] = best_point["value"]
    self._optimisation_data[iteration]["best_coord"] = best_point["coord"]
    self._optimisation_data[iteration]["best_value"] = best_point["value"]

    # compute total time taken
    total_time = time.time() - start_time
    self._optimisation_data["total"]["time_elapsed"] = total_time
    self.config.logger.info(
        "EGO Sequential Optimisation completed in " f"{total_time:.2f} seconds."
    )

    # return the best point
    return best_point

def evaluate_point(
    self, point: dict, inplace: bool = False, bypass_delay: bool = False
) -> dict:
    """Evaluate a given point using the objective function.

    Parameters
    ----------
    point
        A dictionary containing the point to be evaluated.
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, "fid": int})
    inplace
        If True, the evaluation result is added to the input point dictionary.
        If False, a new dictionary is returned with the evaluation result.
    bypass_delay
        If True, the delay specified will be skipped.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A dictionary containing the evaluated point and its objective value.
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, "fid": int, 'value': float})
    """
    # Add starting time to point if not already present
    if inplace:
        if "start_time" not in point:
            point["start_time"] = time.time()
        if MPI is not None:
            point["mpi_rank"] = MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank()
        else:
            point["mpi_rank"] = 0
    elif not inplace:
        evaluated_point = copy.deepcopy(point)
        if "start_time" not in evaluated_point:
            evaluated_point["start_time"] = time.time()
        if MPI is not None:
            evaluated_point["mpi_rank"] = MPI.COMM_WORLD.Get_rank()
        else:
            evaluated_point["mpi_rank"] = 0

    fidelity = point["fid"]
    func = self.config.functions[fidelity]
    value = func(point["coord"])[0]
    if inplace:
        point["value"] = value
    else:
        evaluated_point["value"] = value

    # Pause if a function delay is set
    function_delay = self.config.get("function_delay", None)
    if function_delay is not None and not bypass_delay:
        if len(function_delay) == 0:
            delay = None
        elif fidelity < len(function_delay):
            delay = function_delay[fidelity]
        else:
            # Fewer delays than fidelities: use the delay of the last fidelity
            delay = function_delay[-1]
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"No function delay given for fidelity {fidelity} "
                f"(function_delay has {len(function_delay)} entries); using the "
                f"last value ({delay} s)."
            )
        if delay is None:
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"No function delay found for fidelity {fidelity}. "
                "No delay will be applied."
            )
        else:
            time.sleep(delay)

    if inplace:
        point["end_time"] = time.time()
        return point
    else:
        evaluated_point["end_time"] = time.time()
        return evaluated_point

def get_optimum(self, fidelity: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Retrieve the current optimum from the surrogate model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fidelity
        The fidelity level of the optimum (0 = HF).

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A dictionary containing the optimum information.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the fidelity level is out of range.
    """
    # Check if fidelity is valid
    if fidelity < 0 or fidelity >= self.config.num_fidelities:
        msg = f"Fidelity {fidelity} is out of bounds."
        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    # Check if the optimum of the current model has been calculated before
    if self._trained and self._optimum[fidelity] is not None:
        return self._optimum[fidelity]

    # Check if the model is trained
    if not self._trained:
        self.train()

    # Get the constraints
    # scipy_constr = self.config.scipy_constraints(
    #     return_inexpensive=True, return_surrogate=True
    # )

    result = differential_evolution(
        lambda x: self.predict_values(np.array([x]), fidelity=fidelity),
        self.config.bounds,
        # constraints=scipy_constr,
        strategy=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_strategy", "best1bin"),
        maxiter=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_max_iterations", 1000),
        popsize=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_population_size", 15),
        tol=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_tolerance", 0.01),
        mutation=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_mutation", (0.5, 1)),
        recombination=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_recombination", 0.7),
        disp=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_verbose", False),
        polish=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_polish", True),
        init=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_init", "latinhypercube"),
        atol=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_atol", 0),
        seed=self.config.get("random_seed"),
    )
    self._optimum[fidelity] = {"coord": result.x, "value": result.fun}
    return self._optimum[fidelity]

def add_training_data(self, points: list[dict] | dict) -> None:
    """Add training data to the surrogate model.

    This adds the provided points to the current samples. If you want to
    replace the current samples, use set_training_data instead.

    Parameters
    ----------
    points
        A list of dictionaries containing the training data points.
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, 'fid': int, 'value': float})
        or a dictionary containing the training data points, with fidelity levels as
        keys.
        ({fid: list of dict, ...})
    """
    if isinstance(points, dict):
        points_list = []
        for fid_points in points.values():
            points_list.extend(fid_points)
    else:
        points_list = points

    for point in points_list:
        # Copy the point so the caller's data is not changed
        point = dict(point)
        fidelity = point.get("fid")

        if isinstance(point["value"], list) or isinstance(
            point["value"], np.ndarray
        ):
            point["value"] = float(np.atleast_1d(point["value"])[0])

        self.samples.setdefault(fidelity, [])

        try:
            if any(
                np.array_equal(point["coord"], existing_point["coord"])
                for existing_point in self.samples[fidelity]
            ):
                self.config.logger.info(
                    f"Point {point} already exists in samples for fidelity "
                    f"{fidelity}, not adding."
                )
                continue
        except ValueError as e:
            msg = (
                f"Error checking if point {point} exists in samples for "
                f"fidelity {fidelity}, skipping point (error: {e})."
            )
            self.config.logger.error(msg)
            continue
        self.samples[fidelity].append(point)

    self._trained = False
    self._optimum = dict.fromkeys(range(self.config.num_fidelities), None)

def save_model_to_file(self, file_path: str | pathlib.Path) -> None:
    """Save the surrogate model to a file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_path
        The path to the file where the model should be saved.

    model_data = self.save_model()

    path = pathlib.Path(file_path)

    if path.name == "":
        self.config.logger.error(
            "No file name provided in file path for saving model, "
            "saving to surrogate_model.pkl."
        )
        path = path / "surrogate_model.pkl"

    if path.suffix.lower() != ".pkl":
        if path.suffix != "":
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"File extension not .pkl. Overwriting extension in file name "
                f"{path.name}."
            )
        else:
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"No file extension provided. Adding .pkl to file name, new file "
                f"name: {path}."
            )
        path = path.with_suffix(".pkl")

    parent = path.parent
    if str(parent) not in ("", "."):
        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        pickle.dump(model_data, f)

    self, x: np.ndarray, *args, return_variance: bool = True, **kwargs

    x = self._correct_x_shape(x)

    )
    return (results_val, results_var)

def train(self) -> None:
    """Train the HK surrogate model using the provided training data.

    The lowest fidelity model is trained first, followed by higher fidelity models.
    The training process involves optimising hyperparameters using differential
    evolution and calculating necessary matrices for predictions.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a fidelity level has fewer than 2 samples.
    LinAlgError
        If the regression matrix is ill-conditioned at the optimal hyperparameters.
    """
    # Check if there are enough samples for each fidelity
    fidelities_with_insufficient_samples = [
        fid
        for fid in range(self.config.num_fidelities)
        if len(self.samples[fid]) < 2
    ]
    if fidelities_with_insufficient_samples:
        msg = (
            f"Not enough samples to train HK surrogate at fidelities: "
            f"{fidelities_with_insufficient_samples}. "
            f"At least 2 samples are required per fidelity."
        )
        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    for fidelity in reversed(range(self.config.num_fidelities)):
        x_samples = np.array([p["coord"] for p in self.samples[fidelity]])
        x_samples = self._correct_x_shape(x_samples)
        y_samples = np.array([p["value"] for p in self.samples[fidelity]]).reshape(
            -1, 1
        )

        if fidelity == self.config.num_fidelities - 1:
            # Train the base KRG model
            krg_model = self._model[fidelity]

            krg_model.set_training_values(x_samples, y_samples)
            krg_model.train()
            self._model[fidelity] = krg_model
            continue

        # Train the HK model for the current fidelity
        # 1. Calculate F, y_samples and n
        n = len(x_samples)
        f = self._predict_mean(x_samples, fidelity=fidelity + 1)
        self._model[fidelity] = {
            "y_samples": y_samples,
            "f": f,
            "x": x_samples,
        }

        # 2. Optimise the negative log-likelihood function for theta using
        # differential evolution
        theta_bounds = self.config.get("surrogate.theta_bounds")

        # Convert to log-space bounds for optimisation
        bound_tuple = (np.log(theta_bounds[0]), np.log(theta_bounds[1]))
        bounds = [
            bound_tuple
            for _ in range(np.array(self.samples[fidelity][0]["coord"]).shape[0])
        ]
        dynamic_popsize = max(15, int(40 / self.config.dimension))

        # define a wrapper for the de optimisation
        def _de_wrapper(
            theta_log: float, n_in: int = n, fidelity_in: int = fidelity
        ) -> float:
            """A wrapper function for the objective of DE optimisation.

            Parameters
            ----------
            theta_log
                The natural logarithm of the hyperparameters theta.
            n_in
                The number of samples at this fidelity.
            fidelity_in
                The fidelity level of the model being trained.

            Returns
            -------
            float
                The negative log-likelihood, or 1e12 for invalid theta values.
            """
            theta = np.exp(theta_log)  # Convert back to original space
            log_likelihood = self._log_likelihood_hk(theta, n_in, fidelity_in)

            if log_likelihood is None or np.isnan(log_likelihood):
                return (
                    1e12  # Return a large number to penalise invalid theta values
                )
            return -1 * log_likelihood

        # Start a multi-start to find the optimal theta
        best_neg_ll = np.inf
        n_starts = self.config.get("surrogate.n_theta_optim_starts")
        theta_opt = None
        base_seed = self.config.get("random_seed") + 1
        for i in range(n_starts):
            result = differential_evolution(
                _de_wrapper,
                bounds,
                args=(n, fidelity),
                strategy="rand1bin",
                popsize=dynamic_popsize,
                init="latinhypercube",
                recombination=0.9,
                mutation=(0.5, 1.2),
                tol=1e-8,
                polish=True,
                seed=base_seed + i,
            )

            if result.fun < best_neg_ll:
                best_neg_ll = result.fun
                theta_opt = np.exp(result.x)  # Convert back to original space
                self.config.logger.debug(
                    f"Start {i}: New best Neg-LL found: {best_neg_ll}"
                )

        # 3. Compute the trained model parameters via Cholesky + QR
        try:
            corr_matrix = self._calculate_corr_matrix(x_samples, theta=theta_opt)
            chol = cholesky(corr_matrix, lower=True)
            ft = solve_triangular(chol, f, lower=True)
            q, g = qr(ft, mode="economic")
            yt = solve_triangular(chol, y_samples, lower=True)

            sv = np.linalg.svd(g, compute_uv=False)
            rcond_g = sv.min() / sv.max() if sv.max() > 0 else 0.0
            if rcond_g < 1e-10:
                raise LinAlgError(
                    f"Ft is ill-conditioned (rcond={rcond_g:.2e}) at "
                    f"theta_opt={theta_opt}."
                )

            # beta_0 = (F^T R^-1 F)^-1 F^T R^-1 y solved as G^-1 Q^T Yt
            beta_0_vec = solve_triangular(g, q.T @ yt, lower=False)
            beta_0 = beta_0_vec.item() if beta_0_vec.size == 1 else beta_0_vec

            # sigma^2 = ||C^-1 (y - beta_0 F)||^2 / n
            rho = yt - ft @ np.atleast_2d(beta_0_vec)
            sigma_sq = np.array([[(rho.T @ rho).item() / n]])

            # Precompute gamma = R^-1 (y - beta_0 F) for cheap mean prediction
            residual = y_samples - beta_0 * f
            gamma = solve_triangular(
                chol.T,
                solve_triangular(chol, residual, lower=True),
                lower=False,
            )
        except (LinAlgError, ValueError) as e:
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"Unstable matrix at fidelity {fidelity} during training "
                f"({e}); falling back to a degenerate HK fit at this level."
            )

            chol = np.eye(n)
            ft = f.copy()
            q, g = (
                qr(ft, mode="economic")
                if np.any(f)
                else (
                    np.eye(n, 1),
                    np.array([[1.0]]),
                )
            )
            beta_0 = 1.0
            sigma_sq = np.array([[1.0]])
            gamma = y_samples - beta_0 * f

        # 4. Store the trained model parameters
        self._model[fidelity].update(
            {
                "beta_0": beta_0,
                "chol": chol,
                "ft": ft,
                "q": q,
                "g": g,
                "gamma": gamma,
                "theta": theta_opt,
                "sigma_sq": sigma_sq,
            }
        )

    # Set the trained flag to True
    self._trained = True
    num_samples = [
        (fid, len(self.samples[fid])) for fid in range(self.config.num_fidelities)
    ]
    samples_summary = "; ".join(
        f"fidelity {fid}: {count} sample{'s' if count != 1 else ''}"
        for fid, count in num_samples
    )
    total = sum(count for _, count in num_samples)
    self.config.logger.debug(
        f"HK surrogate model training completed; total {total} "
        f"sample{'s' if total != 1 else ''}; {samples_summary}"
    )

def predict_variance(
    self, x: np.ndarray, *args, fidelity: int = 0, **kwargs
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Predict variances using the MFK model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x
        Input coordinates for prediction.
    fidelity
        The fidelity level to predict (0 = HF).

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Predicted variances as a numpy array.
    """
    if not self._trained:
        self.train()

    # Check x shape
    x = self._correct_x_shape(x)

    self._check_fidelity(fidelity)
    if fidelity == 0:
        return self._model.predict_variances(x)

    # Column of this fidelity in SMT's levels (0 = lowest fidelity)
    smt_column = self.config.num_fidelities - fidelity - 1
    variances_all_levels = self._model.predict_variances_all_levels(x)[0]
    return variances_all_levels[:, smt_column].reshape(-1, 1)

def get_optimum(self, fidelity: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Retrieve the current optimum from the surrogate model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fidelity
        The fidelity level of the optimum (0 = HF).

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A dictionary containing the optimum information.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the fidelity level is out of range.
    """
    # Check if fidelity is valid
    if fidelity < 0 or fidelity >= self.config.num_fidelities:
        msg = f"Fidelity {fidelity} is out of bounds."
        self.config.logger.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    # Check if the optimum of the current model has been calculated before
    if self._trained and self._optimum[fidelity] is not None:
        return self._optimum[fidelity]

    # Check if the model is trained
    if not self._trained:
        self.train()

    # Get the constraints
    # scipy_constr = self.config.scipy_constraints(
    #     return_inexpensive=True, return_surrogate=True
    # )

    result = differential_evolution(
        lambda x: self.predict_values(np.array([x]), fidelity=fidelity),
        self.config.bounds,
        # constraints=scipy_constr,
        strategy=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_strategy", "best1bin"),
        maxiter=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_max_iterations", 1000),
        popsize=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_population_size", 15),
        tol=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_tolerance", 0.01),
        mutation=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_mutation", (0.5, 1)),
        recombination=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_recombination", 0.7),
        disp=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_verbose", False),
        polish=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_polish", True),
        init=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_init", "latinhypercube"),
        atol=self.config.get("surrogate_opt_atol", 0),
        seed=self.config.get("random_seed"),
    )
    self._optimum[fidelity] = {"coord": result.x, "value": result.fun}
    return self._optimum[fidelity]

def add_training_data(self, points: list[dict] | dict) -> None:
    """Add training data to the surrogate model.

    This adds the provided points to the current samples. If you want to
    replace the current samples, use set_training_data instead.

    Parameters
    ----------
    points
        A list of dictionaries containing the training data points.
        ({'coord': np.ndarray, 'fid': int, 'value': float})
        or a dictionary containing the training data points, with fidelity levels as
        keys.
        ({fid: list of dict, ...})
    """
    if isinstance(points, dict):
        points_list = []
        for fid_points in points.values():
            points_list.extend(fid_points)
    else:
        points_list = points

    for point in points_list:
        # Copy the point so the caller's data is not changed
        point = dict(point)
        fidelity = point.get("fid")

        if isinstance(point["value"], list) or isinstance(
            point["value"], np.ndarray
        ):
            point["value"] = float(np.atleast_1d(point["value"])[0])

        self.samples.setdefault(fidelity, [])

        try:
            if any(
                np.array_equal(point["coord"], existing_point["coord"])
                for existing_point in self.samples[fidelity]
            ):
                self.config.logger.info(
                    f"Point {point} already exists in samples for fidelity "
                    f"{fidelity}, not adding."
                )
                continue
        except ValueError as e:
            msg = (
                f"Error checking if point {point} exists in samples for "
                f"fidelity {fidelity}, skipping point (error: {e})."
            )
            self.config.logger.error(msg)
            continue
        self.samples[fidelity].append(point)

    self._trained = False
    self._optimum = dict.fromkeys(range(self.config.num_fidelities), None)

def save_model_to_file(self, file_path: str | pathlib.Path) -> None:
    """Save the surrogate model to a file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file_path
        The path to the file where the model should be saved.
    """
    model_data = self.save_model()

    path = pathlib.Path(file_path)

    if path.name == "":
        self.config.logger.error(
            "No file name provided in file path for saving model, "
            "saving to surrogate_model.pkl."
        )
        path = path / "surrogate_model.pkl"

    if path.suffix.lower() != ".pkl":
        if path.suffix != "":
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"File extension not .pkl. Overwriting extension in file name "
                f"{path.name}."
            )
        else:
            self.config.logger.warning(
                f"No file extension provided. Adding .pkl to file name, new file "
                f"name: {path}."
            )
        path = path.with_suffix(".pkl")

    parent = path.parent
    if str(parent) not in ("", "."):
        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        pickle.dump(model_data, f)

def update_number_of_points(self, number_of_points: int) -> None:
    """Update the number of points in the configuration.

    Parameters
    ----------
    number_of_points
        The new number of points to set in the configuration.
    """
    if number_of_points < 1:
        self.config.logger.warning(
            "Number of new points must be at least 1. Not changing."
        )
        return

    self.config["number_new_points"] = number_of_points

Singleton class to manage the settings used.

This class is used to define the problem to be solved, including: - The lower and upper bounds of the problem - The functions to be used in the optimisation - The constraints to be used in the optimisation - The settings for the optimisation process

It exposes properties for: - lb: The lower bound of the problem - ub: The upper bound of the problem - bounds: The combination of the bounds - functions: The list of functions to be used in the optimisation - constraints: A dict containing a list of equality and a list of inequality constrains - inequality constraints: A list of the inequality constraints. - equality constraints: A list of the equality constraints. - valid_keys: The list of valid setting keys

It also exposes methods for: - get_setting: Get a setting value - get: Get a setting value using dot notation - set_setting: Set a setting value using dot notation - get_function: Get a specific function - update_settings: Update the settings - update_used_algorithms: Update the used algorithms and re-validate settings - validate_bounds: Static method to validate the bounds

Retrieving and updating settings can be done in several ways: - Using get_setting and set_setting methods x = config.get_setting('max_iter', algorithm='optimisation') config.update_settings('max_iter', 200, algorithm='optimisation') - Using get and set methods with dot notation x = config.get('optimisation.max_iter') config.set('optimisation.max_iter', 200) - Using indexing operator overloads getitem and setitem x = config['optimisation', 'max_iter'] config['optimisation', 'max_iter'] = 200

def __init__(
    self,
    used_algorithms: dict,
    lb: np.ndarray | list[float],
    ub: np.ndarray | list[float],
    functions: list[Callable],
    inexpensive_constraints: dict | None = None,
    expensive_constraints: dict | None = None,
    settings: dict | None = None,
    logger: logging.Logger | None = None,
    name: str = __name__,
) -> None:
    """Initialise the Settings singleton class.

    Parameters
    ----------
    used_algorithms
        A dictionary containing the algorithms being used.
        Allowed keys are:
        - 'optimisation': str
        - 'infill': str
        - 'surrogate': str
    lb
        The lower bound of the problem ([x1, x2, ..., xn])
    ub
        The upper bound of the problem ([x1, x2 ..., xn])
    functions
        The list of functions to be used in the optimisation, ordered from HF to LF
    inexpensive_constraints
        A dict containing the constraints. The dict has two possible keys:
        equality and inequality. Each containing a list of constraint functions.
        If None no constraints will be used.
        These constraints will be used as is and will be directly used.
    expensive_constraints
        A dict containing the constraints. The dict has two possible keys:
        equality and inequality. Each containing a list of constraints. Each
        constraint is a list of Callable constraints, ordered from HF to LF.
        If None no expensive constraints will be used.
        From these constraints a surrogate will be created, which will be used in
        the optimisation. This surrogate will be updated throughout the optimisation
        process.
    settings
        A dictionary containing the settings to initialise with.
        If None, default settings will be used.
    logger
        The logger instance to use. Defaults to the module-level logger.
    name
        The name of the Config instance.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If used_algorithms has keys other than 'optimisation', 'infill' and
        'surrogate', no functions are given, the bounds are invalid, the constraints
        are malformed, or expensive constraints are given with an infill strategy
        that does not support them.
    """
    if logger is None:
        logger = get_logger()

    # Config is a singleton. A new Config(...) call defines a new problem, so
    # re-initialise the existing instance instead of silently keeping the old
    # problem definition. Clear all instance state to avoid stale attributes.
    if getattr(self, "_initialised", False):
        self._logger.warning(
            "Config was already initialised; re-initialising it with the new "
            "arguments. Objects that hold this Config now see the new problem. "
            "Call Config.destroy_instance() first to make this explicit."
        )
        self.__dict__.clear()

    # Initialise logger
    self._logger = logger

    if any(
        key not in ["optimisation", "infill", "surrogate"]
        for key in used_algorithms
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "used_algorithms can only contain the keys: "
            "'optimisation', 'infill', 'surrogate'."
        )
    self._used_algorithms = used_algorithms
    self._settings = {}

    # Check functions
    if not functions:
        raise ValueError("At least one function should be provided.")

    # Wrap the functions, so every function returns a 1D float array (a function
    # may also return a plain float) and calls are logged in debug mode.
    if self._logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):
        self._logger.debug("Debug mode enabled, logging every function call.")
    self._functions = [
        self._wrap_objective(func, idx) for idx, func in enumerate(functions)
    ]

    self._constraints = {
        "inexpensive": {"equality": [], "inequality": []},
        "expensive": {"equality": [], "inequality": []},
    }
    for constraint_type, value in [
        ("inexpensive", inexpensive_constraints),
        ("expensive", expensive_constraints),
    ]:
        if value is not None:
            if not isinstance(value, dict):
                msg = (
                    f"{constraint_type}_constraints should be a dict with keys "
                    f"'inequality' and 'equality'."
                )
                self.logger.error(msg)
                raise ValueError(msg)
            for key in value.keys():
                if key not in ["inequality", "equality"]:
                    msg = (
                        f"Invalid key ({key}) in {constraint_type}_constraints "
                        "dict, only 'inequality' and 'equality' are allowed."
                        "Ignoring this key."
                    )
                    self.logger.warning(msg)
            self._constraints[constraint_type] = {
                "inequality": value.get("inequality", []),
                "equality": value.get("equality", []),
            }

    # Check that the infill strategy supports expensive constraints. Empty
    # constraint dicts or lists count as no constraints.
    if any(self._constraints["expensive"].values()) and (
        used_algorithms.get("infill", None)
        not in EXPENSIVE_CONSTRAINT_COMPATIBLE_INFILL
    ):
        msg = (
            "Expensive constraints are provided but the selected infill "
            f"algorithm ({used_algorithms.get('infill', None)}) is "
            f"not compatible with expensive constraints. Please select an infill"
            f" algorithm from the following list: "
            f"{EXPENSIVE_CONSTRAINT_COMPATIBLE_INFILL}."
        )
        self.logger.error(msg)
        raise ValueError(msg)

    self._scipy_constraints = []
    for key, value in self._constraints["inexpensive"].items():
        n_constr = len(value)
        if key == "equality" and n_constr > 0:
            self._scipy_constraints.append(
                NonlinearConstraint(
                    fun=self._vectorise(value),
                    lb=np.zeros(n_constr) - 1e-8,
                    ub=np.zeros(n_constr) + 1e-8,
                )
            )
        elif key == "inequality" and n_constr > 0:
            self._scipy_constraints.append(
                NonlinearConstraint(
                    fun=self._vectorise(value),
                    lb=-np.inf * np.ones(n_constr),
                    ub=np.zeros(n_constr),
                )
            )

    self._expensive_constraint_surrogates: dict[str, list[Callable]] = {
        "inequality": [],
        "equality": [],
    }
    self._expensive_constraint_surrogates_scipy: dict[str, NonlinearConstraint] = {}

    # Check bounds
    if isinstance(lb, list):
        lb = np.array(lb)
    if isinstance(ub, list):
        ub = np.array(ub)
    self.validate_bounds(lb, ub)
    self._lb = lb
    self._ub = ub

    if settings:
        self.update_settings(settings)
    else:
        # update settings with default values
        self._settings = validate_settings(
            settings=self._settings,
            used_algorithms=self._used_algorithms,
            logger=self.logger,
        )

    self._dot_settings = self._flatten_settings(self._settings)

    # Seeded random generator shared by the components (instead of seeding the
    # global NumPy random state)
    self._rng = np.random.default_rng(self._settings["random_seed"])

    # Set the name
    self.name = name

    # Set the initialised flag
    self._initialised = True

def set_bounds(self, lb: np.ndarray | list, ub: np.ndarray | list) -> None:
    """Update both bounds in one call.

    The lb and ub setters each validate the new bound against the current other
    bound, so moving the whole domain (e.g. from [0, 1] to [2, 3]) is not possible
    one bound at a time. This method validates the new bounds together.

    Parameters
    ----------
    lb
        The new lower bound ([x1, ..., xn])
    ub
        The new upper bound ([x1, ..., xn])
    """
    if isinstance(lb, list):
        lb = np.array(lb)
    if isinstance(ub, list):
        ub = np.array(ub)
    self.validate_bounds(lb, ub)
    self._lb = lb
    self._ub = ub

def constraints(self, return_surrogate: bool = False) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Get all constraints.

    Parameters
    ----------
    return_surrogate
        Whether to return the surrogates of the expensive constraints. If False, the
        real functions are returned

    dict[str, dict]
        The constraints, as a dict with the keys ``'expensive'`` and
        ``'inexpensive'``. Each holds
        ``{'inequality': [...], 'equality': [...]}``.
    """
    if return_surrogate:
        return {
            **self._constraints,
            "expensive": self._expensive_constraint_surrogates,
        }
    return self._constraints

def scipy_constraints(
    self, return_inexpensive: bool = True, return_surrogate: bool = False
) -> list[NonlinearConstraint]:
    """Get the inexpensive constraints in a format for scipy optimisers.

    Parameters
    ----------
    return_inexpensive
        Whether to return the inexpensive constraints.
    return_surrogate
        Whether to return the surrogate constraints.

    Returns
    -------
    list[NonlinearConstraint]
        A list of the constraints formatted for scipy optimisers.
    """
    if return_surrogate and return_inexpensive:
        return self._scipy_constraints + list(
            self._expensive_constraint_surrogates_scipy.values()
        )
    if return_surrogate and not return_inexpensive:
        return list(self._expensive_constraint_surrogates_scipy.values())
    if not return_surrogate and return_inexpensive:
        return self._scipy_constraints
    return []

def update_settings(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
    """Handle the update of settings.

    Possible inputs:
    - dict: a dictionary with key-value pairs
        (possibly nested for optimisation, infill, surrogate)
    - key: string, value: any: a single key-value pair to update in the top level
    - key: string, value: any, algorithm: string: a single key-value pair to update
        in a specific algorithm section (eg: 'optimisation', 'infill', 'surrogate')

    Parameters
    ----------
    *args
        See notes above
    **kwargs
        See notes above
    """
    if args and len(args) == 1 and isinstance(args[0], dict):
        settings_dict = args[0]
        for key, value in settings_dict.items():
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                if key not in self._settings:
                    self._settings[key] = {}
                for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
                    self._settings[key][sub_key] = sub_value
            else:
                self._settings[key] = value

    elif len(args) == 2:
        key = args[0]
        value = args[1]
        if "algorithm" in kwargs:
            algorithm = kwargs.pop("algorithm")
            self._settings[algorithm][key] = value
        else:
            self._settings[key] = value

    elif "key" in kwargs and "value" in kwargs:
        key = kwargs.pop("key")
        value = kwargs.pop("value")
        algorithm = kwargs.pop("algorithm", None)

        if algorithm is None:
            self._settings[key] = value
        else:
            self._settings[algorithm][key] = value

    # Validate the settings after update
    self._settings = validate_settings(
        settings=self._settings,
        used_algorithms=self._used_algorithms,
        logger=self.logger,
    )

    # Update the dot notation settings
    self._dot_settings = self._flatten_settings(self._settings)

def validate_bounds(lb: np.ndarray, ub: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Staticmethod which raises a ValueError if the bounds are not correct.

    Parameters
    ----------
    lb
        the lower bound ([x1, ..., xn])
    ub
        The upper bound ([x1, ..., xn])

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the bounds have different lengths, or ub <= lb in any dimension.

    lb = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(lb, dtype=float))
    ub = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(ub, dtype=float))

        raise ValueError("Not all ub > lb.")

@classmethod
def from_json(cls: "Config", input_settings: str | dict) -> "Config":
    """Create the singleton instance from a JSON file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    input_settings
        The path to the JSON file or the loaded json as a dict.

    Returns
    -------
    Config
        The singleton instance.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If n_fidelities is 0 or negative.
    """
    if isinstance(input_settings, dict):
        input_dict = input_settings
    else:
        input_dict = None
        with open(input_settings, "r") as f:
            input_dict = json.load(f)
    resulting_config_dict = input_dict.copy()

    # import the function
    module_name = input_dict["functions"]["module"]
    try:
        function_module = importlib.import_module(module_name)
    except ModuleNotFoundError as e:
        msg = f"Could not import the function module '{module_name}': {e}."
        if module_name == "mf2":
            msg += (
                " mf2 is an optional dependency; install it with "
                'pip install "multi-fidelity-multi-point-sbo[benchmarks]".'
            )
        get_logger().error(msg)
        raise ModuleNotFoundError(msg) from e

    if input_dict["functions"]["module"] == "mf2":
        function_set = getattr(
            function_module,
            input_dict["functions"]["attribute"].lower().replace(" ", "_"),
        )
    else:
        function_set = getattr(
            function_module, input_dict["functions"]["attribute"]
        )()

    n_functions = input_dict["functions"].get("n_fidelities", None)

    clamp_msg = None
    if n_functions is not None and n_functions > len(function_set.functions):
        clamp_msg = (
            f"n_fidelities={n_functions} is larger than the "
            f"{len(function_set.functions)} available fidelities; "
            "using all of them."
        )
    if n_functions is None or n_functions >= len(function_set.functions):
        resulting_config_dict["functions"] = function_set.functions
    elif n_functions <= 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "Currently 0 or a negative number of functions are to be used, "
            "this is an invalid setting."
        )
    else:
        resulting_config_dict["functions"] = function_set.functions[:n_functions]
    resulting_config_dict["lb"] = np.array(function_set.l_bound)
    resulting_config_dict["ub"] = np.array(function_set.u_bound)

    # Import the constraints if given
    if "constraints" in input_dict and input_dict["constraints"]:
        constraint_module = importlib.import_module(
            input_dict["constraints"].pop("module")
        )
        for key in ["inequality", "equality"]:
            if key in input_dict["constraints"]:
                constraint_funcs = []
                for func_name in input_dict["constraints"][key]:
                    constraint_func = getattr(constraint_module, func_name)
                    constraint_funcs.append(constraint_func)
                resulting_config_dict["constraints"][key] = constraint_funcs

    # Set up the logger
    if "logger_instance" in input_dict:
        logger_instance = input_dict["logger_instance"]
        resulting_config_dict["logger"] = logger_instance
        resulting_config_dict.pop("logger_name", None)
        resulting_config_dict.pop("logger_instance", None)

    elif "logger_name" in input_dict:
        logger_instance = get_logger(
            name=input_dict.get("logger_name", __name__),
            **input_dict.get("logger", {}),
        )
        resulting_config_dict.pop("logger_name", None)
        resulting_config_dict["logger"] = logger_instance

    elif isinstance(input_dict.get("logger"), dict):
        # Logger settings without a name: use them for the default logger
        resulting_config_dict["logger"] = get_logger(**input_dict["logger"])

    if clamp_msg is not None:
        (resulting_config_dict.get("logger") or get_logger()).warning(clamp_msg)

    return cls(**resulting_config_dict)
